assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only three-days-of-happiness:substitute-watcher@original-novel#novel-monograph (the canonical v1.0 substitute-watcher novel monograph, qualified COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY (bounded) with standalone self-containment PASS and sampled primary-source fidelity PASS and no material correction, according to the discovery row) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the single Japanese witness TDH-JP-01; its close evidence is Ch12 P0004-P0173, Ch14 P0155-P0168 and Miyagi's report at Ch15 P0089-P0105. The subject is the unnamed man who substitutes for Miyagi, distinct from the woman who appraises Kusunoki's second sale. The monograph's marker do_not_use_as_literary_evidence and its statement that it is a literary portrait, not a behavioral reconstruction, were read as method inputs, as were the completion audit's original gate-2 row (minor figures, one to three scenes, no differentiated portrait), its later bounded qualification and its statement that no reconstruction operation is authorized. The readings, the longitudinal notebook, the synthesis, the audit and the Kusunoki, Miyagi, Himeno and Shinbashi monographs are not cited, and nothing is borrowed from them. No translation, adaptation or other edition is assessed, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The two days of substitution in Ch12 (arrival and antagonism P0004-P0023; questions about Miyagi and her records P0025-P0041; Kusunoki's confession and the notebook P0042-P0049; the night walk and stated motive P0061-P0070; the spending question and withheld price P0080-P0103, with Kusunoki's later recollections at P0147-P0157 and P0163-P0173), the accompaniment to Kusunoki's second sale (Ch14 P0155-P0168), and Miyagi's report of his relay and procedure (Ch15 P0089-P0105) as her testimony. His handling of the purchase of Miyagi's time when she was ten is his own statement (Ch12 P0025-P0041). States are split at the softening after he skims the notebook (Ch12 P0042-P0049, P0080-P0083). Nothing about him after Ch15 P0105 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph centers the substitute watcher on selective intervention: he presses for answers while withholding them (the spending question and the withheld price, Ch12 P0080-P0103), shows explicit concern for Miyagi and makes his treatment of Kusunoki sound conditional on it (P0025-P0041), and gives an unusually direct statement of purpose, that he watches by choice to come near others' deaths so he may accept his own (P0061-P0070). Strongest counterevidence: routine duty explains much of his conduct, and he judges Miyagi's first sale harshly yet handles her last, a tension the text leaves unresolved. Not C: why he softens after the notebook, whether he approved either final sale and how care and duty weigh are open, so the evidence cannot tell which motive decides; that is insufficiency. Not E: a stated purpose and a recurring withholding pattern across Ch12 and Ch14 give more than one local fact.

One located change in the substitute watcher: from contempt for Kusunoki's leisure (Ch12 P0004-P0023) to qualified attention after Kusunoki's confession and the notebook (P0042-P0049, P0080-P0083), with the cause left open and the notebook's contents unknown. The later shop scene and Miyagi's report are brief. Not D: no development traced beyond that one shift.

With Kusunoki the substitute watcher speaks in blunt colloquial contractions and familiar, often abrasive address, calls Miyagi ano ko, and modulates within the one relationship: a grudging qualification, sharp contempt, a quieter account of his contact with Miyagi, candid reflection about his death, and ridicule joined to a precise limit on disclosure (Ch12 P0007-P0040, P0063-P0070, P0080-P0101). The monograph states that his register to Miyagi, in their correspondence and toward other subjects is not evidenced. Not D: one addressee over two days, with no worded rows.

Located ordinary conduct of the substitute watcher is limited to scrutinizing and dismissing the vending-machine album and the paper cranes, lunch, the night walk and his stated practice of asking every subject what they did with the proceeds (Ch12 P0004-P0023, P0061-P0070, P0080-P0083). Not D: no routine beyond the two days of duty.

Toward Kusunoki, the substitute watcher moves from critic to limited confidant, and his treatment is stated as conditional on how Kusunoki has treated Miyagi (Ch12 P0025-P0049). Toward Miyagi he is a remote colleague with documentary access who expressly denies closeness (two or three written exchanges; watchers cannot see each other) and, by her report, an effective procedural intermediary (Ch15 P0089-P0105). Not D: one relationship is observed directly, over two days; the Miyagi relation rests on his statements and her testimony.

The substitute watcher's interior is available only through his statements in Kusunoki's record: his concern for Miyagi, his denial of having sold time, health or lifespan, and his reason for watching (Ch12 P0025-P0041, P0061-P0070). The monograph treats the motive as self-report, not evidence that his plan works. Not D: no other access.

Located conflict conduct of the substitute watcher: open criticism of Kusunoki's use of his remaining life (Ch12 P0004-P0023); on Kusunoki's confession he looks about to grab him but does not, in Kusunoki's account (P0042-P0049); sarcasm and a refusal to say more about the price (P0080-P0101). Not D: few cases, one of them in Kusunoki's reading of a gesture.

Ethically weighted positions of the substitute watcher are located: he says Miyagi could not have judged normally at ten and calls her situation pitiable (Ch12 P0025-P0041); he deliberately brings the sale price into question without vouching for a conclusion (P0080-P0103); and, by Miyagi's report, he handles the procedure of her own final sale after she has decided (Ch15 P0089-P0105). Not D: the text gives no account of how he weighs these, and whether he approved either final sale is not shown.

The substitute watcher's humor is sarcasm and ridicule: the jab about whether he would get sympathy (Ch12 P0061-P0070), laughter at Kusunoki's banknote distribution with two corrections of Kusunoki's reading of why he laughed (P0080-P0103). Not D: few instances, all with Kusunoki.

The monograph covers every passage in which the substitute watcher appears or is reported (Ch12 P0004-P0173, Ch14 P0155-P0168, Ch15 P0089-P0105), routes them to notebook IDs (TDH-S065-S067, S080, S084; TDH-C035, C057, C060, C061, C069, C071) and readings U12, U14 and U15, and keeps him distinct from the appraiser; the discovery row records standalone and sampled primary-source fidelity checks that passed without material correction. Not B: the portrait is short, its check sampled, and part of his role rests on Miyagi's report. Not D: his complete presence is covered and checked.

The evidence affirmatively bounds the substitute watcher: he denies being close to Miyagi; he denies having sold time, health or lifespan; he says he did not read the notebook in detail; he refuses to give the real price; he is surprised by the second valuation and is not the appraiser who speaks about Kusunoki's future (Ch14 P0155-P0168); and in Miyagi's report she had already decided on her sale before he handled it. Not B: few situations. Not D: located denials and contrary facts, not only silence.

The substitute watcher's scenes are anchored by paragraph across two days in Ch12, the shop in Ch14 and the report in Ch15, with the softening placed after the notebook. Not B: short spans with relative timing, and Miyagi's report places his role without dating it. Not D: an explicit, anchored sequence.

scenario_readiness.note: The substitute watcher's register is sampled only toward Kusunoki over two days, and the monograph states that his speech to Miyagi, in writing or toward other subjects is not evidenced. Illustrative lines beyond the located exchanges would be underdetermined.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The two days of substitution in Ch12 (split at the softening after the notebook), the shop in Ch14 P0155-P0168, and Miyagi's report at Ch15 P0089-P0105 as her testimony; nothing after Ch15 P0105.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kusunoki as the subject he watches in Miyagi's absence; Miyagi only as a remote colleague known through records, his statements and her report; the woman appraiser only as present at the second sale.
setting_constraints: The novel's world, with him on duty as a watcher
Kusunoki's apartment, the walks and the shop as located; no off-duty life, other subjects or institutional offices
No primary-source reading beyond the cited monograph

scenario_readiness.note: The motives that would decide the substitute watcher's conduct in a new situation (care or duty, approval of the sales, why he softened) are open, and the evidence is a few scenes. A novel scenario can only be checked against the located conduct.
Only two days of duty with Kusunoki are shown; the substitute watcher's ordinary social conduct is not characterized beyond them.
The substitute watcher's ethically weighted acts are located, but how he weighs them, and whether he approved either final sale, are not shown; deliberation in a new situation would be invention.
Nothing about the substitute watcher's romantic life is recorded.

The substitute watcher's work is shown at the level of conduct (substituting, consulting records, accompanying a sale), but the institution's procedures, his discretion and any fee are not established, and his role in Miyagi's sale is her report.

known_limits.statement: The substitute watcher is unnamed and appears in two days of Ch12, briefly in Ch14 and in Miyagi's report in Ch15; the novel gives no employment history or independent view of the deaths he says he wants to encounter.
Why the substitute watcher softens toward Kusunoki is open: the notebook's contents are never revealed, and he says he did not read it in detail.

Whether the substitute watcher approved either final sale is not shown; he judges Miyagi's first sale harshly yet is reported to handle her last, and the text gives no conversion, sanction or private endorsement.
The substitute watcher's relay to Miyagi and his handling of her sale are her report, not a witnessed scene; his knowledge of her plan before she decided is not exposed.
The substitute watcher's speech is sampled only toward Kusunoki; his register to Miyagi and toward other subjects is not evidenced.
The cited evidence contains no reconstruction model, probe or evaluation of the substitute watcher; the monograph describes itself as a literary portrait, not a behavioral reconstruction.
